long_biography.plain_text:
Elisabeth Max-Theurer's partnership with Mon Cherie turned an initially difficult horse into a European champion and, in 1980, an Olympic dressage winner. She had begun riding as a child in Linz and developed under trainer Hans Max, whom she later married. Max-Theurer subsequently represented Austria at two further Olympic Games and carried the flag at the 1992 opening ceremony.

After retiring from competition, she remained inside the sport as an international dressage judge and Olympic administrator. She serves as a vice-president of the Austrian Olympic Committee. She also breeds dressage horses, including Augustin OLD, whom her daughter Victoria rode at Olympic, European and World championship level.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative name, nationality and birth date align exactly with official Olympic and FEI records, while company and registry sources add the distinctive founder-daughter and family-shareholding bridge. No public source reviewed explicitly names Max-Theurer as owner of the selected private vessel, so residual uncertainty concerns only that non-public relationship.

The official 2025 company report gives Max-Theurer a 37.5 per cent direct holding-company stake. A registry filing entered on the research date replaces the direct family shareholders at that company with JMT Holding-FlexCo, whose official register still names Elisabeth, Victoria and Johannes as shareholders. The free official extract does not state their post-reorganisation economic percentages, so the dossier describes a continuing family interest without treating the earlier direct percentage as current.

Founder Josef Theurer is documented as Max-Theurer's father, and an institutional source shows father and daughter held company shares concurrently before his death. The family-transfer mechanism is therefore positively established, but the legal instrument and timing are not. Marriage / family transfer is used at medium confidence; Inherited and Inherited and expanded would overstate the record.

Current company and registry material separates Max-Theurer's family shareholding from her son Johannes's management mandate. Heir / family shareholder captures that distinction without inferring passivity beyond the industrial group or overlooking her extensive operating leadership in equestrian sport.

Many otherwise reliable profiles still call Max-Theurer president of the Austrian Equestrian Federation. Current April 2026 reporting establishes that Herbert Gugganig succeeded her after a 24-year tenure, so the dossier treats that presidency as completed while retaining her 2025-elected Austrian Olympic Committee vice-presidency as current.

An exact-name LinkedIn profile belongs to a Croatia-based Schiffahrt in Brioni employee and was excluded. The existing Wikipedia link is retained, and only Plasser & Theurer's official company site is proposed.
